name: Side By Side
label: Revelation
lede: They lasted about a year and a half, broke up before their only record came out, and that seven-song 7" has been pressed again and again for nearly four decades.

eras.title: Five months from first show to first band
eras.text: Jules Massee, a kid from Weehawken, New Jersey, saw his first hardcore show on Long Island in the early summer of 1986. Within about five months he was fronting a band out of an Alphabet City apartment, part of the youngest wave of the New York straight edge crowd.

years.h: Jules Massee's first hardcore show: the Right Track Inn
years.p: Jules Massee's introduction to hardcore is a Right Track Inn bill on Long Island with [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]], [[Straight Ahead|1fd60d7c-dc35-44f5-9162-4113b6ca4a69]] and [[Sick of It All|e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7]].

years.h: Side By Side starts in an Alphabet City apartment
years.p: Jules Massee sings, Eric Fink plays guitar and Billy Bitter plays bass, with drummer Gavin borrowed from NY Hoods for the early stretch.

years.h: [[Sammy Siegler|869c662b-574c-46ac-acf6-3dc6f025fd5a]] takes over Side By Side's drums
years.p: Sammy Siegler, born in 1973, is barely into his teens when he joins Side By Side. He'll go on to play in Youth of Today, [[Judge|3827fbb6-e219-4e2d-9af8-35cc9a7d8d8e]], [[Gorilla Biscuits|0320a32e-b781-40df-bf48-5cb5ee842762]] and CIV.

eras.title: On the first Rev roll call
eras.text: Revelation Records' second release gathered the new straight edge New York bands on one 7", and Side By Side were on it. They played the same bills as Youth of Today, Gorilla Biscuits and Warzone all year, then went into Don Fury's studio.

years.p: Side By Side's first appearance on record, on Revelation's second release. The first press was 600 black and 400 orange, the orange being the 'gold' vinyl collectors still confuse with the later yellow.

years.h: Kids push the bouncers off the CBGB stage
years.p: After a lawsuit, CBGB's owner hires bouncers to stop stage diving. At the first note of Gorilla Biscuits' set, Jules Massee says, the kids bum-rush them off the stage, and the matinees are briefly halted.

years.h: [[Alex Brown|bc640ea8-3500-4100-876e-6ad2b33b0390]] joins Side By Side on second guitar
years.p: Alex Brown completes Side By Side's line-up and soon joins Gorilla Biscuits too. He isn't on the band's EP: Jules Massee says it was cut by the original four.

eras.title: Gone before the record came out
eras.text: Side By Side drifted apart after the session, with no fight and no big final night planned as one. The record landed after the band was already over, and the members were already feeding the next wave of bands.

q: It wasn't poetic, it wasn't complicated... but it was genuine.
years.src: In Effect Hardcore · Wikipedia: Youth of Today
years.h: Side By Side's last show: the Anthrax, and their best
years.p: Side By Side's final official show is at the Anthrax, a club in Connecticut, and the band remembers it as the best they ever played.
years.xp:
There was no dramatic ending. The members simply drifted apart, and You're Only Young Once... was already recorded.

Sammy Siegler landed in Youth of Today within months, and Alex Brown was already playing in Gorilla Biscuits.

years.h: You're Only Young Once... comes out after the band splits
years.p: Side By Side cut the seven-song EP with [[Don Fury|0bec484f-b890-4823-af64-0e48530f6f6f]] in 1987. Revelation released it as REV 5 in 1988, after the band had already broken up.
years.xp:
Guilty, Good Clean Fun and a Youth Brigade cover never got recorded. The first press came in two batches of 1,005 and 1,012, pressed about a week apart, some with one of at least three stickers.

Two more 2,000-copy presses followed: silver labels with the cover opening at the bottom on the second, grey labels and a black border around the back-cover live photo on the third.

years.h: Side By Side, Gorilla Biscuits and Bold live at the Anthrax, Norwalk CT, January 15, 1988
yt: Side By Side, Gorilla Biscuits and Bold live at the Anthrax, Norwalk CT, January 15, 1988

years.h: Jules Massee plays a benefit for [[Roger Miret|ab51d57f-5007-4ee4-8461-a4050f8d939d]]
years.p: Jules Massee is back on the CBGB stage at a benefit show for [[Agnostic Front|40b8a690-94e4-4c82-ad0f-73f4b841e46a]] singer Roger Miret.
About a year after Side By Side split, Jules Massee starts Alone in a Crowd with [[Lars Weiss|c60d8790-7786-4df8-8647-7f8b2ca02c17]], who'd go on to Uppercut and Judge.

eras.title: The record that kept getting pressed
eras.text: With the band long gone, You're Only Young Once... became a Revelation evergreen. The label kept bringing it back on new colors of vinyl, and Alex Brown became a painter whose work reached MoMA.

years.h: You're Only Young Once... on 12" for the first time
years.p: Revelation's first 12" edition of Side By Side's EP: 1,109 on black vinyl and 100 on blue.
Revelation presses 550 copies of You're Only Young Once... on red vinyl, followed by grey in 2013 and gold in 2017.

years.h: Side By Side guitarist Alex Brown dies at 52
years.p: Alex Brown died suddenly of a basal ganglia stroke, Civ said, correcting early reports of an aneurysm. By then he was a painter shown in New York, Tokyo, Geneva and Brussels.
years.xp: He is remembered through the Alex Brown Foundation, an artist residency in Des Moines, Iowa, where he was born.

eras.title: Three is a magic number
eras.text: Jules Massee, by now a lawyer in Florida, had no plans to play again. A benefit for late guitarist Alex Brown brought the originals back for three shows across two continents, and they called the last one the last.

q: I never had any intention of playing with Side By Side again.
years.h: Side By Side reunite for Alex Brown
years.p: Jules Massee, Eric Fink, Billy Bitter and Sammy Siegler, with Lars Weiss on second guitar, play Revolution Calling in the Netherlands in late November, for the Alex Brown Foundation.
years.xp:
Weiss had played bass at the band's last show in the '80s; this time he took Brown's guitar spot. Massee's conditions, he told No Echo, were the original line-up and a charitable purpose in Brown's memory, and proceeds went to the Alex Brown Foundation.

Massee was the least likely to say yes. He said the reunion came in threes, and left it at that.

years.h: Side By Side headline a benefit at the Monarch, Brooklyn
years.p: Side By Side headline a benefit show at the Monarch in Brooklyn, thirty-five years after You're Only Young Once... came out.

years.h: Reunion set at Revolution Calling, November 25, 2023
yt: Reunion set at Revolution Calling, November 25, 2023

years.h: Side By Side's final show: The Book of Revelation Records, L.A.
years.p: On night two of Revelation's weekend at 1720 in Los Angeles, Side By Side share the bill with Youth of Today in what's billed as their final reunion show.
